source.title: Feature Integration Spaces: Joint Training Reveals Dual Encoding in Neural Network Representations

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses polysemanticity and proposes that some features encode computational relationships, but it does not test the neuron-pole audit or any of the specific claim versions. Its experiments concern SAE/NFM features, not the share of neurons with one or two identifiable jobs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own experiments on SAE/NFM integration features, recorded below as findings related to the claim's subject but not covered by a claim version. It does not audit neuron poles or test explanation quality on held-out activations. Mentioned results from other work, including prior SAE reconstruction findings, are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAE/NFM dictionaries on OpenLLaMA-3B layer 16 and probes secondary SAE 'integration' features with clamping. It never audits individual neurons or neuron poles, never scores neuron explanations on held-out text, and builds no neuron-based attribution graphs. Its argument that polysemanticity may encode meaningful relations is conceptual. It is not tested on neurons, and InceptionV1 is not examined. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also emphasize that joint SAE+NFM training gives a 41.3% reconstruction improvement and a 51.6% reduction in KL-divergence error, with bimodal feature organization by squared norm. They propose that polysemanticity may reflect meaningful computational roles rather than interference.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sequential and jointly optimized SAE/NFM architectures and intervenes on their learned features; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or held-out neuron-explanation evaluation described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention effects vary with the clamping value; the paper reports separate p-values for -4.0, 0.0, and 4.0.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping secondary SAE feature 4022 in OpenLLaMA-3B produced a formality×emotion interaction in category logits (F=5.06, p=0.027). Linear-component clamping and the non-sensitive feature 1113 showed no such interaction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some SAE 'integration' features in an NFM pathway have selective, nonlinear behavioural effects under factorial stimulus interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: Secondary feature 2020 had its highest activation (0.517) in the formal/emotional condition, with less interaction effect than feature 4022.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Secondary SAE features differ in their activation and interaction profiles across designed semantic conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Max-activation analysis of the integration features returned conjunctions or punctuation rather than interpretable patterns, despite functional effects shown by clamping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features with causal behavioural effects can be uninterpretable by max-activating examples. This concerns SAE features, not neurons.

record.problems: Experiments use one 3B model and one stated middle layer; the paper describes its intervention exploration as not exhaustive. It also says integration features remain difficult to interpret directly and that maximum-activation analysis did not yield interpretable patterns for them.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct results about neuron-pole interpretability or explanation performance were reported. Reconstruction and KL-divergence results concern the proposed SAE/NFM architecture, not a measure named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares (about 90% one job, 7% two related jobs, 2–4% not understood).
Interpretable-neuron shares in other dense and MoE models and across scale.
Reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic neurons such as InceptionV1's cat/car neuron.
Interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture, regularization and tools.
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Analysis is of SAE features on one 3B model at one layer, not raw neurons. The integration features were opaque to max-activation inspection, which is loosely related to V6, but they are SAE features and no explanation-to-activation prediction test is run. The peer-review venue in the record is unverified from the text.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B audit shares for one-job, two-related-job, and not-understood neuron poles.
Interpretable-neuron shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and the proposed pose/recursive-generalization interpretation.
The fraction of interpretable neurons under different architectures or tools, including the InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and comparison with a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict other activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
